headline: Humans are social animals—we accomplish more together than any individual could alone
universal_truth: Isolation is weakness; connection is strength; we're built to need each other
fun_facts: Solitary confinement is considered psychological torture because humans need social connection
No individual knows how to make a pencil from scratch—it requires forests, mines, factories, and global logistics
Social connection is as important for health as exercise and nutrition
discussion_questions: What could you never accomplish alone?
When has being part of a group amplified your abilities?
What's the cost of going it alone?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: A single human is remarkably fragile. We can't outrun predators, we can't survive winter alone, we can't make anything complex by ourselves. But together? We've built cities, crossed oceans, walked on the moon. Together, we're unstoppable.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Modern culture celebrates individual achievement. But almost everything valuable requires others. Why are humans so dependent on cooperation?
cliff.prompt: Why do humans need each other?

options.text: We evolved as social animals—our survival depended on groups, so cooperation is wired into our biology and psychology
options.response: Yes. Humans survived not by being the strongest or fastest, but by cooperating better than any other species. Isolation isn't independence—it's vulnerability.

options.text: Modern society requires specialization, so we trade skills
options.response: Trade is part of it, but our need for connection is deeper than just practical exchange...

q1.title: Evolved for Groups
q1.script: Humans evolved in groups of 50-150 people. Exile meant death. Our brains developed to navigate social complexity—reading faces, understanding intentions, maintaining relationships. We're social animals to our core.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Evolved for Groups"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Collective Knowledge
q2.script: No individual knows how to make a smartphone, build a plane, or cure a disease. Knowledge is distributed across millions of specialists. Your daily life depends on expertise you'll never have. We're nodes in a network, not self-sufficient islands.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Connection as Health
q3.script: Loneliness is as harmful as smoking. Social connection affects immune function, mental health, and longevity. We don't just enjoy connection—we require it for health. Relationships aren't luxury; they're necessity.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Isolation is weakness; connection is strength. We're built to need each other. Invest in relationships—they're infrastructure for everything else.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 201. Tomorrow, we'll explore when people disagree—conflict. Until then, appreciate someone who makes your life possible.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Connection Appreciation - Who Enables You?
growTrack.activity: List five people who make your life possible—from close relationships to distant service providers. Thank one of them today. Recognizing our interdependence is the first step toward gratitude and better collaboration.
